bottom_line: In 7601 patients with chronic heart failure, candesartan vs placebo reduced cardiovascular death or hospital admissions for CHF (adjusted hazard ratio 0.82 [0.75–0.88]).
implications: These data support that, in this broad chronic heart-failure population, candesartan reduced cardiovascular death or hospital admissions for CHF versus placebo (0.82 [0.75–0.88]) and reduced cardiovascular deaths (0.87 [0.78–0.96]). All-cause mortality showed an adjusted reduction (0.90 [0.82–0.99]) while the unadjusted result was borderline (p=0.055). The numbers also show more discontinuations for hypotension/creatinine/hyperkalaemia with candesartan, so the benefit estimates apply alongside these reported tolerability differences.

major_points.text: Programme design: parallel randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials across three LVEF/ACE-inhibitor-defined populations.
major_points.quote: In parallel, randomised, double-blind, controlled, clinical trials we compared candesartan with placebo in three distinct populations.

major_points.text: Dose and allocation: candesartan titrated to 32 mg once daily vs matching placebo, with 7601 patients randomised.
major_points.quote: Overall, 7601 patients (7599 with data) were randomly assigned candesartan (n=3803, titrated to 32 mg once daily) or matching placebo (n=3796)

major_points.text: Overall programme primary outcome was all-cause death.
major_points.quote: The primary outcome of the overall programme was all- cause death.

major_points.text: Primary outcome for each component trial was cardiovascular death or unplanned admission to hospital for worsening CHF.
major_points.quote: The outcomes in the three component trials were: cardiovascular death or unplanned admission to hospital for the management of worsening CHF (primary outcome)

major_points.text: All-cause mortality result: 886 (23%) vs 945 (25%), adjusted hazard ratio 0.90 [0.82–0.99], p=0.032.
major_points.quote: 886 (23%) in the candesartan group and 945 (25%) in the placebo group died from any cause (unadjusted hazard ratio 0·91 [95% CI 0·83–1·00)], p=0·055; covariate adjusted 0·90 [0·82–0·99], p=0·032

major_points.text: Cardiovascular deaths were fewer with candesartan: 691 (18%) vs 769 (20%), adjusted hazard ratio 0.87 [0.78–0.96].
major_points.quote: cardiovascular deaths: 691 (18%) in the candesartan compared with 769 (20%) in the placebo group (unadjusted 0·88 [0·79–0·97], p=0·012; covariate adjusted 0·87 [0·78–0·96], p=0·006

major_points.text: Safety/tolerability: more permanent discontinuations due to hypotension, increased creatinine, and hyperkalaemia with candesartan.
major_points.quote: discontinued candesartan than placebo because of concerns about renal function, hypotension, and hyperkalaemia.

guidelines_referenced.quote: American Heart Association. Heart disease and stroke statistics: 2003 updates.

inclusion_criteria.text: Women and men aged 18 years or older with symptomatic heart failure (NYHA class II–IV) for at least 4 weeks’ duration.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Eligible patients were women and men aged 18 years or older who had symptomatic heart failure (New York Heart Association class II–IV) for at least 4 weeks’ duration.

exclusion_criteria.quote: Major exclusion criteria included serum creatinine 265 ␮mol/L or more, serum potassium 5·5 mmol/L or more, known bilateral renal artery stenosis
Major exclusion criteria included serum creatinine 265 ␮mol/L or more, serum potassium 5·5 mmol/L or more, known bilateral renal artery stenosis, symptomatic hypotension

criticisms.text: Subgroup analyses are cautioned to be interpreted carefully; authors state the most rigorous test comes from the entire population.
criticisms.quote: Subgroup analyses must be interpreted cautiously since the most rigorous test of the study hypothesis is derived from the entire population

criticisms.text: Authors state they cannot determine whether survival improvement was related to target dose or other pharmacological properties.
criticisms.quote: However, we cannot tell to what extent this improvement in survival was related to the 32 mg daily target dose of candesartan or other potentially distinctive pharmacological properties.
